---
title: "Subidized Facility Location"
description: ""
resources:
  - widget.html
---

Suppose each vertex $v$ of a graph $G = (V, E)$ carries a hidden, independent
Bernoulli random variable $Y_v$ with known $\Pr[Y_v = 1] = p_v$. You cannot look
at the vertices. What you *can* do is probe an edge $e = (u, v)$, which reveals
the edge variable

$$
X_{uv} = Y_u \vee Y_v ,
$$
